title: Multi scale simulation of water rock interaction: from experimental optimization to long-term prediction of geothermal reservoirs
description: Publication date: Available online 31 August 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Longyuan Lu, Guoyang Liu, Peng Zhang, Xiaoxiao Yin
abstract: The influence of rock–water interaction processes on heat transfer efficiency during the long-term operation of Enhanced Geothermal Systems (EGS) remains poorly understood, which highlights the necessity of systematic research on geochemical evolution and its impact on reservoir performance. Based on single-fracture water-rock reaction experiments and core-scale reactive transport models, relevant reaction kinetic parameters were calibrated and optimized, and a site-specific reactive solute transport model was established by integrating geological characteristics of the study area. A 35-year long-term simulation was carried out to systematically analyze the spatiotemporal evolution of dissolved solute concentrations in geothermal fluids, focusing on the dynamic changes of key solutes (including SiO2, Na+, K+) and their response to water-rock reactions. The results confirm that feldspar dissolution is the core driver of solute concentration changes and reservoir geochemical evolution, while biotite and anorthite, due to their low content and weak reactivity, have no significant impact on the overall geochemical process and solute transport. SiO2 precipitation, as a secondary factor, only causes local changes without affecting the overall geochemical evolution trend dominated by feldspar dissolution. This study clarifies the intrinsic relationship between water-rock reactions, solute concentration changes and geothermal fluid evolution, provides a reliable theoretical basis and technical support for the long-term stable operation of EGS.

title: Palaeoenvironmental evolution and organic matter enrichment in the Early Silurian Yangtze Foreland Basin: Tectonosequence stratigraphic insights for shale gas exploration
description: Publication date: Available online 28 August 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Xinguo Li, Rui Liu, Yuxuan Wang, Junwei Pu, Hui Liu, Lu Xu, Tongtong Luo, Xiucheng Tan, Weiming Chen, Ruiying Chao
abstract: Although large amounts of organic-rich marine shale were deposited in the foreland basin, the mechanisms governing organic matter enrichment remain debated. The Early Silurian Longmaxi shale in the Upper Yangtze Block provides critical insights into the mechanisms of organic-matter enrichment within a foreland basin. This study integrates seismic stratigraphy, sedimentology, and geochemistry to unravel the influence of tectonic and depositional dynamics on organic matter enrichment. The Longmaxi shale, deposited within a transgressive system tract, is bounded at the top by a maximum flooding surface (MFS) marked by a silty-laminated mudstone unit with a high gamma-ray peak in the lower part of a low gamma-ray response, and at the base by an angular unconformity at the Ordovician-Silurian boundary formed during forebulge migration. The Longmaxi shale consists of four parasequences, with pinch-out lines migrating northwestward toward the Chuanzhong Forebulge Uplift, reflecting westward progradation driven by high sediment flux from the Cathaysia Block. Redox-sensitive proxies (Corg/P and MoEF/UEF ratios) reveal a vertical shift from anoxic (Parasequences 1–2) to suboxic (Parasequences 3–4) conditions during the Rhuddanian sea-level rise; meanwhile, nutrient flux indicators (P and Baex concentrations) show an upward increase of primary productivity. Generally, total organic carbon (TOC) content correlates strongly with the redox-sensitive (Corg/P ratio) and sedimentation rate (Ti, Al) proxies, but weakly with the primary productivity proxy, Baex concentration. These patterns suggest that organic matter enrichment in the Early Silurian Longmaxi shale of the Upper Yangtze Block was primarily controlled by deepwater oxygen level and inorganic particle dilution. Deglaciation-driven freshwater input enhanced watermass circulation and deepwater oxygenation, thus reducing the preservation efficiency of organic matter, particularly in the foredeep adjacent to the Cathaysia Block. Additionally, although elevated sedimentation rates enhanced primary productivity via increased nutrient supply, dilution by inorganic detrital particles markedly reduced organic matter abundance in the foredeep. These findings highlight that high-quality shale gas reservoirs were most likely developed in intervals characterized by persistent anoxia and minimal detrital dilution, providing a predictive framework for sweet spot identification in foreland basin settings.

title: Mineralogy and Elemental Geochemistry of Coal Seams from underground fire-affected Jharia coal fields: Environmental Significance
description: Publication date: Available online 28 August 2026 Source: Applied Geochemistry Author(s): Sukalyan Chakraborty, Wasim Akram Shaikh, Robert Barry Finkelman, Abhishek Kumar, Naomi Ty Asha Nichols
abstract: Uncontrolled coal fires in the Jharia coalfield, India, are examples of one of the worst forms of anthropogenic pollution, as they introduce a broad range of geotoxic compounds into the environment. This study examined the occurrence and distribution of fluoride and heavy metals in fire-affected villages of the Jharia region in various environmental media - coal, soil, plants, condensates/ sublimates, standing water, and foliar dust. The levels of fluoride were extraordinary, 411-622 mg kg-1 in coal, 166-147,333 mg kg-1 in condensates, 328-415mg kg-1 in soils, and 134-150 mg L-1 in water samples- way above the normal levels found in the environment. Fe (up to 37,070 mg kg-1), and Zn (268-449 mg kg-1) were highly enriched, and Mn, Mg, Cr, Cu, and Pb were moderately enriched. Geo-statistical indices showed that there is extreme Fe pollution (Igeo = 6.44-7.43) and moderate Zn contamination (Igeo = 1.09-1.30), PLI value (1.59-2.23). The highest bioaccumulation factor (BAF) for fluoride was observed in Ageratum conyzoides (9.34) and Croton bonplandianum (5.47), indicating that they are potential accumulator. The results indicate that during combustion of coal, volatilized minerals, such as fluorapatite, contribute to extensive contamination of the atmosphere and soil in the immediate vicinity, posing a high ecological and human health risk, particularly in areas with high concentrations in the condensates. Further, the hazard quotients and hazard indices (HI) were <1, indicating no significant non-carcinogenic health risk under the assessed exposure conditions. In addition, the elevated carcinogenic risk was observed in some selected condensate samples. There should be continuous monitoring and remediation measures that will reduce fluoride and heavy metal exposure in this susceptible coal-mining area.

title: Response of mercury in sediments to environmental change in the Western Arctic Ocean since the late last deglaciation
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Song Zhao, Chao Cui, Weibin Zhang, Yanguang Liu
abstract: Since the last deglaciation, the western Arctic Ocean shelf has undergone a dramatic environmental transition from subaerial exposure to marine inundation. Permafrost, widely formed across the Arctic during the Last Glacial Maximum and acting as a vast reservoir of both organic carbon and mercury (Hg) during glacial periods, is highly sensitive to climate warming. The opening of the Bering Strait and the associated sea-level rise since the Late Pleistocene have fundamentally reshaped the sedimentary environment of the Chukchi Sea, which in turn influenced the burial and redistribution of Hg. However, how sedimentary Hg records have responded to this process remains unclear. This study analyzes a sediment core from the Chukchi Sea shelf in the western Arctic Ocean, spanning approximately the last 13 ka, to reconstruct the long-term evolutionary history of Hg burial fluxes. Our results reveal that, sedimentary Hg fluxes in the Chukchi Sea shelf increased by a factor of 4.4 from the last deglaciation to the late Holocene, primarily driven by the combined effects of remobilized Hg release, enhanced burial, and increased deposition. The region experienced two distinct peaks in Hg release during the early and late Holocene, driven by fundamentally different mechanisms. The early Holocene peak primarily resulted from the release and burial of Hg associated with permafrost organic carbon during transgression, coupled with extensive coastal erosion and thermokarst activity. The second, the Hg flux peak was closely linked to sea-ice retreat events driven by enhanced Pacific Water inflow during the late Holocene. Increased advection of warm Pacific waters extended the open-water season, enhancing the efficiency of the biological pump. This, in turn, facilitated the scavenging of water-column Hg by marine-derived organic carbon and likely enhanced the oceanic uptake of atmospheric Hg(0), thereby boosting the overall marine Hg sink. We note, however, that owing to the finite and trace nature of Hg in the environment, Hg burial might have been primarily supply-limited, potentially making the Hg flux less sensitive to environmental changes during periods of low atmospheric/oceanic Hg availability. The pre-anthropogenic natural background record revealed in this study elucidates the stepwise response of Hg burial on the Arctic shelf to climate forcing. It highlights the response of permafrost activation and ocean biogeochemical dynamics in governing the burial fate of this pollutant, providing a historical analog for assessing the evolution of the Arctic Hg.

title: Hydrothermal activity in the Eocene rift lake of the Beibuwan Basin, South China Sea: Mineralogical and geochemical constraints from lacustrine mudrocks
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Jiahao He, Qian Huang, Dujie Hou, Xinde Xu, Xiong Cheng, Gang Zhou, Weijun He
abstract: Hydrothermal fluids are important carriers of material and energy exchange among Earth spheres, yet well-documented records of their activity in ancient lacustrine basins remain limited. We conducted backscattered electron-energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy imagery, elemental geochemical and strontium isotope analysis of Eocene lacustrine mudrocks from the Beibuwan Basin (BBWB). The results show that the shales contain abundant euhedral pyrite aggregates, chalcopyrite, native gold, siderite, and euhedral dolomite, indicating syngenetic hydrothermal activity. Coordinated positive excursions in Fe, Mn, P, Cu, Ba and Zn concentrations, paired with positive europium anomalies (δEu), record two short-lived diffuse flow events in the lower member of the Liushagang Formation (LS3) and a focused flow following deposition of the middle member of the Liushagang Formation (LS2). Tectonic analysis suggests that the remote effects of the India-Eurasia collision at ∼50 Ma potentially triggered basement fault activity, creating favorable pathways for hydrothermal fluid migration. Cross-plot of Fe/Ti versus Al/(Al + Fe + Mn) indicates that mudrocks near the basement faults received 20–50% hydrothermal contributions, whereas samples farther from the faults received less than 20%. Sr isotope compositions suggest that the hydrothermal fluids are of the crustal source, and identify two fluid endmembers. One is a high-temperature, reducing, sulfide-rich fluid associated with the syngenetic faults. The other is a carbonate-rich fluid formed in the depocenter via mixing with Upper Paleozoic limestone basement and lacustrine water. Tectonic activity and fault distribution are the main controlling factors for the source and migration of the two fluid types. This study fills the research gap of Eocene hydrothermal activity in the BBWB for the first time. It also provides an analog for hydrothermal sedimentation studies in the South China Sea and other rift lacustrine basins worldwide.

title: Redox and hydrodynamic controls on roll-front sandstone-type uranium mineralization: Insights from reactive transport modeling
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Yongqiang Zou, Zenghua Li, Teng Deng, Chiheng Liu, Yinhang Cheng, Deru Xu, Fei Xia, Lifei Yang
abstract: Roll-front sandstone-type uranium deposits are important uranium resources worldwide, but their orebodies vary significantly in location, geometry and grade despite broadly similar redox-controlled mineralization processes. This variability is attributed to differences in redox conditions, uranium source availability and groundwater flow, yet how these geological factors control orebody variability under hydrodynamic regimes remains poorly constrained. This study is the first to use reactive transport modeling to reproduce the dynamic process of roll-front uranium mineralization and to evaluate the effects of different geological factors on uranium orebody formation. The modeling results demonstrate that the dynamic balance between the reducing capacity of host sandstones and the oxidizing capacity of fluids exerts primary control on the localization, geometry and lateral extent of roll-front orebodies. Both strongly reducing host sandstones and weakly oxidizing fluids can limit interlayer oxidation, favoring narrow, relatively high-grade roll-front orebodies near the recharge area. In contrast, weakly reducing host sandstones and more oxidizing fluids allow significant interlayer oxidation, producing larger but relatively lower-grade mineralized zones farther from the recharge area. The uranium concentration in the fluids and the pre-enriched uranium content of the host sandstones are positively correlated with ore grade and together exert a primary control on the formation of high-grade roll-front uranium orebodies. Groundwater flow rate also exerts a non-linear influence on uranium mineralization, with moderate flow rates most favorable for uranium dissolving in the oxidization zone and reprecipitation at the redox front. Extremely low flow rates limit oxidation-front advance, whereas high flow rates promote extensive oxidation. These findings help explain the geological controls on orebody localization, geometry, and grade variability in roll-front uranium systems and provide a quantitative framework to guide future exploration.

title: Significant boron isotopic variations during crustal reworking recorded in multiple generations of tourmaline in S-type granites, South China
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Wei Li, Shuyun Cao, Eizo Nakamura, Zhong Liu, Tsutomu Ota, Yanlong Dong, Tak Kunihiro
abstract: Metamorphic dehydration and partial melting during crustal reworking play a critical role in the recycling of elements in collisional orogens. While boron (B) has great advantages in deciphering these fluid-related processes, its behavior during sequential evolution of multistage melts/fluids is not fully understood. Here, we investigate these processes through comprehensive analyses of major-trace elements and B isotopes of tourmaline in well-characterized S-type granites from the South China Block (SCB). Different occurrences of tourmaline have been identified, including (i) isolated tourmaline crystals and/or radiating tourmaline clusters with complex zoning pattern (Tur-Ia), (ii) isolated tourmaline crystals with patchy zoning pattern (Tur-Ib), (iii) loosely aggregated tourmaline crystals with complex zoning pattern in tourmaline aggregates (Tur-IIa), and (iv) densely tourmaline aggregated crystals with core-rim zoning pattern in tourmaline aggregates (Tur-IIb). Multiple generations of tourmalines with different origins display clear differences in texture, element, and B isotopic isotopes. Early-magmatic tourmaline is texturally and compositionally homogeneous with Mg/(Mg + Fe) = 0.21 to 0.53, while late-magmatic tourmaline has lower Mg/(Mg + Fe) = 0.03 to 0.44. Tourmaline of fluid origin, which is characterized by dissolution-reprecipitation texture and oscillatory zoning, has a large compositional range with Mg/(Mg + Fe) = 0.02 to 0.87. Chemical compositions of magmatic tourmaline were predominantly controlled by fractional crystallization, while chemical variations of tourmaline of fluid origin are mainly attributed to interaction of magma-derived hydrothermal fluids with metasedimentary rocks and/or addition of Mg-rich external fluids, in part because of the recharge of magma-derived Fe-rich hydrothermal fluids. The δ11B values are in the range of −11.8 ∼ −9.6‰ for early-magmatic tourmaline, in the range of −10.1 ∼ −6.7‰ for late-magmatic tourmaline and in the range of −14.5 ∼ −4.6‰ for tourmaline of fluid origin. We attribute the bimodal distribution of magmatic tourmaline δ11B to the occurrence of multistage tourmaline precipitation during magma differentiation to form an increase in the δ11B of tourmaline crystalized in later stages that assumes a Rayleigh fractionation. The varied B isotopes of tourmaline of fluid origin are controlled by the increase in δ11B formed by boron-isotope fractionation and the decrease in δ11B formed by addition of low δ11B external dehydration fluids, as evidenced by the elemental characteristics of tourmaline of fluid origin with low δ11B and model calculation of B behavior. On this basis, we propose a model where post-collision extension led to metamorphic dehydration of metasedimentary rocks, with the resultant metamorphic fluids not only migrating upward and interacting with overlying metasedimentary rocks to generate a metasomatic source that subsequently underwent dehydration melting to produce granitic melts, but also participating in fluid activity in later stages. A spatiotemporally coupled metamorphic dehydration-partial melting mechanism may result in locally variable B isotope values in syn- and post-collisional magmas through melt-fluid-rock interaction and fluid mixing.

title: Zn isotopic evidence for the role of recycled sedimentary carbonate in generating carbonatites and alkaline rocks associated with rare-metal mineralization
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Juan Wang, Ling Han, Peilong Cui, Yu Kang, Shuaijun Wang, Ganglan Zhang, Xiangfa Wang
abstract: Carbon is crucial to the genesis of carbonatites and alkaline rocks associated with rare metal deposits, yet its origin remains poorly constrained. Here we present an integrated study of petrography, titanite U-Pb geochronology, and whole-rock geochemistry (major and trace elements, Sr-Nd-Zn isotopes) to evaluate the role of recycled sedimentary carbonate in the generation of carbonatite-syenite complex from the Miaoya Nb-REE deposit and the alkaline volcanic rocks from the Yehuzhai Nb deposit, which are spatially related in the South Qinling (SQ) region. The combined titanite U-Pb ages, major and trace elements, and Sr-Nd isotopes indicate that these carbonatites and alkaline rocks were derived from a mantle metasomatized by oceanic crust-derived melts/fluids and formed in an early Paleozoic extensional tectonic setting linked to the opening of the Mianlue Ocean. The Miaoya complex exhibits a wide range of δ66Zn values from 0.29‰ to 0.44‰, with some values higher than those of MORB. A two-end-member mixing model suggests that up to 25% of recycled sedimentary carbonate was incorporated into the mantle source. In contrast, the Yehuzhai alkaline rocks yield MORB-like δ66Zn values (0.29–0.36‰), which can be explained by partial melting of peridotitic mantle with negligible contribution from sedimentary carbonate. The contrasting Zn isotopic signatures reflect the varying degree of recycled carbonate contribution to the mantle heterogeneity beneath the SQ region. Collectively, these findings highlight a genetic relationship among deep carbon cycle, tectonic activity, carbonatite-alkaline rocks generation, and rare metal mineralization.

title: Time-dependent intensity corrections for accurate quantitative point or X-ray mapping analysis by electron microprobe
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Julien M. Allaz, Anette von der Handt, John J. Donovan
abstract: Many materials undergo modifications to both structure and chemistry during electron bombardment in an electron probe microanalyzer (EPMA). This results in changes to the emitted X-ray intensities by various physical processes including heating, breaking of molecular bonds, ionization, volatilization and sputtering, subsurface static charging and subsequent mobility of the measured elements. Most of these processes are proportional to the degree and duration of electron beam exposure (analytical time, acceleration voltage, beam current, and beam focus) and to the thermal and electrical conductivity of the analyzed material. Therefore, quantitative accuracy is dependent upon correction schemes that monitor changes in X-ray emission over time, a process called Time-Dependent Intensity (TDI) corrections. This paper investigates various applications of TDI corrections and demonstrates that accurate point analyses can be obtained with such corrections. Moreover, the combination of replicate X-ray mapping with a TDI correction can produce precise and accurate quantitative element maps for beam-sensitive materials, expanding the range of materials and analytical conditions suitable for EPMA applications.

title: The selenium cycling variation corresponding to the evolution of early animals in the Weng'an biota
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Zhiyuan Ren, Jie Long, Shixi Zhang, Yajun Du, Tengwen Long, Yung-Tsang Chen, Kunli Luo
abstract: The Weng'an biota witnessed the critical expansion and differentiation of early animals in the Ediacaran Period. It shows an enrichment of bioessential elements such as Se and Mo accompanying the expansion of Megasphaera fossils. However, whether the expansion of early animals affected the Se source and its preservation remains unclear. This research focuses on studying the Se speciation and preservation variations in the Weng'an biota along with the occurrence, expansion, and disappearance of Megasphaera fossils and the covariation of redox conditions. Before the Megasphaera occurrence, it shows 14.5% of bioavailable Se(VI) and Se(IV) (29 ppb), 2% (up to 13 ppb) of Se(0), 57% (56 ppb) of Se(II) and 26.5% (40 ppb) of organic Se (Org-Se). The bioavailable Se(VI) and Se(IV) increased to 35% (160–8000 ppb) in the first occurrence datum of Megasphaera while the Se(0), Se(-II), and Org-Se decreased to 1% (155 ppb), 54% (7800 ppb), and 10% (1500 ppb) respectively. The Se(VI) + Se(IV) and Se(-II) changed to 46% (10,000 ppb) and 40% (9200 ppb) respectively within the acme interval of Megasphaera while the proportions of Se(0) and Org-Se remained similar to the occurrence layer. In the decline interval, the Se(VI) + Se(IV), Se(-II) and Org-Se varied to 9% (8 ppb), 76% (56 ppb), and 15% (40 ppb) respectively while the Se(0) became undetectable. After excluding the effects of terrestrial input and hydrothermal activities, we proposed that the Se cycling variation in the Weng'an biota was highly probably related to the evolution of Megasphaera.

title: Competing effects of mantle melting, magma crystallization and degassing on sulfur, chalcophile, and siderophile elements in volcanic glasses from Shatsky Rise and Ojin Rise seamounts
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Maxim Portnyagin, Renat Almeev, Jörg Geldmacher, Roman Botcharnikov, Dieter Garbe-Schönberg
abstract: Oceanic large igneous provinces (LIPs), such as Shatsky Rise in the western Pacific, commonly exhibit variable and locally elevated abundances of chalcophile and siderophile elements (CSEs), reflecting the conditions of mantle melting and subsequent magma differentiation. However, the processes and conditions controlling these enrichments remain poorly understood. To unravel these processes, we analyzed major, volatile, and trace elements, including the strongly chalcophile and siderophile trace and ultra-trace elements Cu, Ag, Se, Re, Pt, Au, and Bi, in 48 glass samples from Shatsky Rise and the adjacent Ojin Rise seamounts. We also determined Fe3+/ΣFe ratios in 19 glasses and measured major element and sulfur contents in plagioclase-hosted melt inclusions from the Tamu Massif, the oldest in the Shatsky Rise. Parental Shatsky Rise magmas are strongly enriched in CSEs relative to MORB. They are inferred to have formed at logfO2 of FMQ to FMQ − 1 and to have evolved by fractional crystallization, resulting in auto-oxidation to as high as FMQ + 1 in the most evolved melts. The CSE patterns of the normal-type Shatsky Rise magmas are consistent with extensive (22–25%) mantle plume melting that exhausted sulfide from the mantle residue. In contrast, parental Ojin magmas resemble MORB and became sulfide-saturated during the early stages of fractional crystallization. They were likely generated by more moderate degrees of mantle melting, leaving a sulfide-bearing residue at logfO2 below FMQ. All Shatsky Rise melts remained sulfide-undersaturated during fractional crystallization down to ∼7 wt% MgO. At lower MgO, the glasses define two contrasting evolutionary trends: sulfur-rich, CSE-depleted, sulfide-saturated compositions from the Ori Massif and Ojin Rise seamounts, and sulfur-poor, CSE-enriched, slightly more oxidized, sulfide-undersaturated compositions from the Tamu Massif. Ori Massif magmas record little or no sulfur degassing during crystallization and eruption and remain to be sulfide-saturated. In contrast, Tamu magmas experienced substantial pre-eruptive sulfur loss within an open-vent magmatic system, where prolonged recycling and mixing of degassed and undegassed magmas progressively depleted the magma in sulfur. These results highlight the fundamental role of shallow magmatic processes in controlling CSEs behavior in oceanic plateau magmas and determine their potential for the formation of magmatic sulfide deposits. Sulfide undersaturation during shallow evolution diminishes the ore-forming potential of LIP magmas, whereas late-stage sulfide saturation favors formation of Au–Cu–PGE-rich but relatively Ni-poor magmatic sulfides.

title: Temporal variations in the Fe isotope composition of Arctic Ocean Fe-Mn crusts reflect iron sources and environmental conditions
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Natalia Konstantinova, Minako Kurisu, James R. Hein, Sergei Skolotnev, Georgy Cherkashov, Katsuhiko Suzuki
abstract: Layered ferromanganese crusts from Mendeleev Ridge and Northwind Ridge in the Arctic Ocean Amerasia Basin, and Vøring Spur and Knipovich Ridge in the North Atlantic Ocean constitute valuable archives of paleoenvironmental changes for the Arctic region. Temporal variation in δ56Fe isotope values of hydrogenetic Fe-Mn crusts from the deep Arctic Ocean vary from 0.00‰ to −0.44‰. Both Amerasia Basin Fe-Mn crusts show relatively heavy late Miocene δ56Fe values (0.00‰ to −0.12‰) followed by a decrease during the Pliocene–Pleistocene, likely reflecting increasing Fe contributions from redox reactions in continental-shelf sediments. The δ56Fe signatures in the uppermost layers of Fe-Mn crusts from the Mendeleev, Northwind and Knipovich Ridges are consistent and their reconstructed seawater compositions agree well with modern dissolved Fe isotope values from comparable depths in Canada Basin and Mendeleev Ridge. The Fe-Mn crust from Vøring Spur indicates a relatively constant Fe source from deep North Atlantic waters since the late Miocene.

title: Copper isotope evidence for Cu transfer during oceanic crust subduction: insights from the (ultra)high-pressure metamorphic belt of Southwestern Tianshan, China
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Yu Chen, Yuanyuan Xiao, Yongxiang Yao, Baptiste Debret, Ziwei Sun, Hongmei Gong, Yao Liu, Kaiyun Chen
abstract: Constraining the behavior of Cu during subduction is the key to decipher processes leading to the porphyry Cu deposit formation at convergent margins, while also shedding light on S cycling owing to the chalcophile affinity of Cu. This study reported δ65Cu values for bulk-rock and chalcopyrite from a metamafic rock from the (ultra-)high pressure metamorphic belt of Southwestern Tianshan, China. The rock consists of abundant glaucophane-dominated breccias (part A) crosscut by a large-scale omphacite-rich vein system (part B) with sharp boundaries. The glaucophane-dominated breccias are interpreted as partially dehydrated metabasalts, while the omphacite-rich vein system reflects the main fluid pathways in the subduction channel. Part A exhibits elevated δ65Cu values (0.07‰ to 0.36‰) and low Cu contents (52 ppm on average) compared to MORB (δ65Cu = 0.04‰ to 0.14‰; Cu = 90 ppm). Together with heavier δ65Cu values of chalcopyrite (−0.17‰ to 0.23‰) in part A compared to magmatic sulfide, these suggest that dehydration preferentially releases isotopically light Cu and leaves residues with heavier Cu isotope compositions. Part B shows complementary light δ65Cu values both in bulk rock and chalcopyrite. The negative correlation between S and δ65Cu indicates that precipitated sulfides complexed with light Cu isotopes may result in lowered δ65Cu values in the rock during fluid-rock interactions. Overall, the data point to the mobilization of isotopically light Cu-bearing fluids during the dehydration of mafic crust in subduction environments. However, the absence of commonly high Cu contents in arc magmas suggests that the released copper may be buffered by sulfides in the sub-arc mantle, resulting in Cu-rich sulfide accumulations.

title: Sulfide inclusions in phenocrysts from basanite lithic clasts and mafic phonolite lapilli from the Upper Laacher See Tephra (Germany): Evolution of an immiscible sulfide liquid
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Alexandre V. Andronikov, Irina E. Andronikova, Ondrej Pour, Gerhard Wörner
abstract: Sulfide inclusions in phenocrysts from phonolite lapilli from the Upper Laacher See Tephra (ca. 13 ka) along with basanite lithic clasts were analyzed in situ for major- and trace-element compositions using SEM and LA-ICP-MS techniques. For the first time, we trace the compositional evolution of trace elements in the Laacher See immiscible sulfide liquids that exsolved from the basanite and mafic phonolite melts at various stages of differentiation. Sulfide inclusions represent former immiscible sulfide liquids that exsolved from both basanite parent magma and evolved daughter phonolite melts. After their incorporation into host minerals, the inclusions in basanitic mafic phenocrysts evolved during ascent and cooling in dikes and/or lava flows. The resultant sulfide inclusions are always polymineralic and composed of Fe-, Cu-, and Ni-rich phases (mainly pyrrhotite, chalcopyrite, pentlandite). In contrast, sulfide inclusions in mafic and felsic phenocrysts in phonolite lapilli are almost pure, homogeneous pyrrhotite (Cu-Ni-poor phase) and have low content of Ni, Co, and Cu, but elevated concentrations of Cd, Pb, Te and Zn. Our data thus document a sequence of sulfide liquid exsolution that occurred along the differentiation path from basanite to phonolite magma.

title: Geochemical indicators of deep fluid dynamics in the Gulf of Patience (Sakhalin Island): new data on submarine mud volcanism and its connection with the region's tectonics
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Varvara Ivanova, Petr Semenov, Anna Kil, Vladimir Slinchenkov, Alexander Kartashev, Vyacheslav Sevastyanov, Boris Vanshtein
abstract: The article presents the results of a comprehensive geochemical monitoring of the underwater gas seep Vostochnoe (the Gulf of Patience, Sea of Okhotsk) in 2022–2025. Based on the analysis of the molecular and isotopic composition (δ13C) of hydrocarbon gases, the distribution of inorganic gases (He, CO₂) and trace elements (Zn, Hg, Cu, Co, Ni, etc.) in bottom sediments, the nature of the fluid system of this feature is characterized for the first time. The composition of gases and sediments of the site is consistent with potential genetic links to the processes feeding the Pugachevsky mud volcano on land, suggesting that the Vostochnoe site may represent its submarine continuation. However, key geochemical indicators (gas dryness coefficient K1, paraversity index K4, helium and mercury contents) suggest possible differences in the discharge mechanism: Vostochnoe is characterized by high thermodynamic maturity of gases, the absence of a typical hydrothermal trace element load, and episodic pulses of deep fluid enriched in helium. Particularly noteworthy is the 2024 anomaly, when a sharp increase in He concentrations (up to 184 ppm) and the appearance of thermogenic methane with δ13С up to −35.6‰ were recorded at several stations, suggesting possible short-term activation of a deep fault. However, these interpretations remain provisional; alternative explanations involving different reservoirs, regional source rocks, or mixing-fractionation effects cannot be excluded without further isotopic and structural studies.

title: Re -Os dating of paleozoic organic-rich black shales by LA-ICP-MS/MS
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Jay M. Thompson, Stijn Glorie, A. Kate Souders, Sarah E. Gilbert, Timothy Paton, Poul Emsbo
abstract: We present a new in-situ method for Re Os geochronology of black shales using LA-ICP-MS/MS that is rapid, cost-effective, and sufficiently accurate and precise to address many geological questions. The method is tested on Paleozoic organic-rich black shales with independently constrained stratigraphic or radiometric ages. Results demonstrate that LA-ICP-MS/MS analysis yields Re Os dates and initial Os isotopic compositions generally within uncertainty of published values using a laser spot size of 100 to 120 μm in diameter. Despite low Os abundances in many samples, high-density microscale sampling compensates through large numbers of analyses, enabling robust inverse isochron regressions. The approach also allows contemporaneous acquisition of trace-element data (V, Ni, Mo and Re), providing insight into metal distribution in a sample, degree of metal enrichments, and serve as a proxy for open-system behavior for Re Os. As a result, LA-ICP-MS/MS ReOs analysis can serve both as a stand-alone geochronological tool and as an efficient screening method prior to conventional ID-N-TIMS, helping to identify optimal intervals and exclude isotopically disturbed material. Together, our study demonstrates that in-situ Re Os geochronology of organic-rich shales is technically viable, geologically informative, and broadly applicable, opening new opportunities to investigate basin evolution, metallogenesis, hydrocarbon systems, and Earth-system processes across deep time.

title: Abundant and diverse Pb nanospheres in polyphase Eoarchean zircon from the Odesa Quarry, Ukrainian Shield
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Monika A. Kusiak, Simon A. Wilde, Richard Wirth, Leonid Shumlyanskyy, Bożena Gołębiowska, Martin J. Whitehouse
abstract: Nanoclusters and nanospheres of radiogenic lead (Pb*) have been recognized in zircon from several locations around the world, but their formation remains enigmatic. Here, we describe examples from the Odesa Quarry in Ukraine that reveal several unique features not previously identified, providing new insights into their origin. Here, randomly distributed Pb nanospheres (cubic crystals of metallic Pb) of various shapes and sizes are present in the cores and rims of zircon, both concordant and discordant, in an Eoarchean quartzitic rock. New features identified include metallic Ti6Pb4.8 (documented earlier only as an experimental product) and composite bodies consisting of Pb nanospheres together with either Ti clusters (in the zircon cores) or with Al (in the zircon rims). These bodies are up to 80 nm in size. In some rim domains, larger Pb nanospheres co-exist with an amorphous silica-rich phase (ASP), either enclosed in a silica globule or margined by silica. This association of Pb nanospheres with either Ti or Al is controlled by the different conditions of zircon growth experienced by the cores and recrystallization of the rims. Such a complexity of Pb mobilization, together with other elements, significantly advances our knowledge about zircon micro- and nanostructures.

title: Resolving two different mantle plume components in the Central Indian Ridge using olivine-hosted melt inclusions from a low-magma supply region
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Sunghwan Im, Jung-Woo Park, Sarang Choi, Jonguk Kim, Andrey A. Gurenko, Seongjun Choi
abstract: Two deep-mantle reservoirs branching from African LLSVP, the Réunion plume and Mascarene Basin Asthenospheric Reservoir (MBAR), have been proposed to influence magmatism along the Central Indian Ridge (CIR), yet distinct geochemical expression, spatial extents and relative contributions remain poorly constrained. In this study, we present major and trace element, volatile and in-situ Pb isotope data for olivine-hosted melt inclusions from a ridge-transform intersection at the CIR 16.5°S where low magma supply preserves primary mantle heterogeneity. The melt inclusions exhibit a broad range of trace element enrichment, collectively encompassing nearly the full compositional variability of the CIR MORB over a distance of ∼1000 km. The melt inclusions are categorized into three types: E-MORB, N-MORB and anomalous melt inclusions. Although some anomalous inclusions show geochemical evidence of interaction with the lower crust and upper mantle, most preserve their primary mantle source signatures. E-MORB melt inclusions exhibit Pb isotopic, halogen, major and trace element compositions suggesting mantle source metasomatized by low-degree melts derived from the Réunion plume. In contrast, N-MORB melt inclusions show restricted La/Sm but wide variability in Pb isotope ratios defining FOZO-DMM array, independent of the Réunion plume signatures. These geochemical characteristics suggests MBAR contribution extends southward to ∼16.5°S as previously inferred from geophysical data. The coexistence of the Réunion plume and MBAR signatures within individual melt inclusions suggests that melt inclusions provide critical role in resolving deep-mantle heterogeneity beneath the Indian Ocean while otherwise remaining cryptic in MORB whole-rocks or glasses, even in low-magma supply regions.

title: In situ iron isotopic analysis of mantle silicate minerals by fs-LA–MC–ICP–MS
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Xinting Lü, Detao He, Yongsheng Liu, Huajiang Liang, Chunfei Chen, Kexin Deng, Xi Zhu, Ming Li, Yansheng Lai, Ao Yang, Jie Lin, Zhaochu Hu
abstract: In situ iron isotope analysis of mantle silicate minerals (e.g., clinopyroxene, orthopyroxene, garnet) is essential for understanding mantle processes. However, existing mineral-scale Fe isotopic data for these phases are predominantly derived from bulk analysis of mineral separates, as in situ measurements are constrained by low iron contents, matrix effects and the lack of suitable reference materials for microbeam analysis. In this study, we present a high-precision method for in situ Fe isotope analysis of silicate minerals using a high-energy femtosecond laser ablation system (GenesisGEO) coupled with MC-ICP-MS. The improved sensitivity enables robust analysis of samples with FeO as low as ∼2.7 wt%. The isobaric interference from 54Cr is accurately corrected using pure Cr metal. Under optimized wet-plasma conditions, a suite of laboratory-synthesized clinopyroxene (CPXA01, CPXB01), orthopyroxene (OPX-GL3), and garnet (GRT-GL3) glasses, along with natural mantle minerals (ML OPX, CUG-OL-Ar, SC Ol), were accurately measured. All materials exhibit homogeneous Fe isotope compositions, making them suitable as in-house quality-control materials. The δ56Fe values obtained by fs-LA-MC-ICP-MS agree with solution data within uncertainty. External reproducibility (2SD) is better than 0.13‰ even at FeO contents below 3 wt%, demonstrating the robustness of the method for analyzing typical mantle silicate minerals. Applying this method to clinopyroxene and garnet from eclogite xenoliths reveals pronounced Fe isotope variability at the micrometer scale, demonstrating its capability to resolve microscale isotopic heterogeneity preserved in mantle minerals. This work extends high-precision in situ Fe isotope analysis from iron-rich sulfides and oxides to major silicate phases of the mantle, thereby enabling micron-scale studies of Fe isotope fractionation during mantle processes.

title: Deciphering the origin of ultrapotassic magmas in the North China Craton: Mg isotopic constraints on the roles of carbonates vs. pelagic clays
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Xiaolu Niu, Yildirim Dilek, Bin Chen, Fei Liu, Shan Ke, Guangying Feng, Jingsui Yang
abstract: The formation of ultrapotassic rocks in subduction zones is a direct consequence of mantle metasomatism by recycled sediments. However, the first-order control exerted by specific sedimentary components (e.g., carbonates vs. pelagic clays) on the compositional diversity of these magmas remains poorly constrained. To address this, we integrate Mg–O–Sr isotopes with elemental geochemistry on a suite of silica-saturated and silica-undersaturated ultrapotassic rocks from the northern North China Craton. These rocks form a coherent geochemical array, characterized by low Hf/Sm (mostly <1) and unradiogenic 87Sr/86Sr (0.705–0.708), alongside high Sr (1000–6000 ppm), Ba (up to 10,000 ppm), and CaO/Al2O3 ratios. This signature precludes a significant contribution from terrigenous sediments but is consistent with a mantle source containing both pelagic clays and carbonates. Critically, Mg isotopes systematically discriminate these sedimentary components. The silica-undersaturated Late Triassic rocks possess light δ26Mg values (−0.42‰ to −0.23‰), requiring modification of their mantle source by carbonatitic melts. In contrast, the silica-saturated Early Devonian rocks exhibit heavier δ26Mg values (−0.27‰ to −0.12‰), implicating pelagic clay as the dominant metasomatic agent. We thus establish a genetic linkage: ultrapotassic magmas from clay-modified sources are silica-saturated and have heavier δ26Mg, while those from carbonate-modified sources are silica-undersaturated and have lighter δ26Mg. This Mg-isotope dichotomy offers a powerful and novel means to trace sediment recycling and unravel the nature of mantle metasomatism in subduction zones.

title: Tracking of the origin and history of fluids in the Hellisheiði and Nesjavellir geothermal fields, Iceland
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Biying Chen, Finlay M. Stuart, Chris M. Holdsworth, Stuart M.V. Gilfillan
abstract: The geochemistry of geothermal fluids provides critical insights into their provenance and subsurface transport mechanisms, which are essential for exploration and sustainable exploitation of geothermal resources. Prolonged production and reinjection of wastewater might overprint original fluid chemistry, complicating reservoir characterisation. This study uses stable isotopes of water (δD, δ18O) and the noble gas composition of production fluids collected during multiple sampling campaigns at the Hellisheiði and Nesjavellir fields, Iceland, to evaluate fluid evolution during continuous production and reinjection. Comparison with pre-commissioning data indicates that water isotopic composition has remained stable, suggesting that production and reinjection have not significantly altered the primary fluid composition over 18 years at Hellisheiði and 34 years at Nesjavellir. The noble gas composition of most samples is consistent with phase separation. The temperature of phase separation constrained by noble gas compositions exceeds surface separator temperatures, suggesting that subsurface boiling has likely occurred. However, the estimated boiling temperatures are 29–145 °C lower than reservoir temperatures, implying that boiling occurs in the shallow subsurface or within the wellbores. This study also provides an evaluation of a Kr tracer test at Nesjavellir that was initiated in 2019, prior to CO2 injection. Measurements made within 330 days of injection failed to detect excess Kr. However, we record excesses of up to 271% relative to the baseline sample. This study reiterates the utility of noble gases as conservative vapour-phase tracers for monitoring subsurface fluid migration and containment of injected fluids.

title: Selenium isotopic constraints on assimilation in layered mafic intrusions: an example from the Northern limb of the Bushveld Igneous Complex
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Sharlotte C. Mkhonto, Matthew I. Leybourne, Heather K. Shrimpton, Pedro J. Jugo, David W. Blowes, Danie F. Grobler, Daniel Layton-Matthews
abstract: The Platreef, located in the Northern Limb of the Bushveld Igneous Complex (BIC) in South Africa, hosts globally significant economic PGE-Ni-Cu mineralization and is characterized by variable interaction of the BIC magmas with Archean granites and Paleoproterozoic Transvaal Supergroup metasedimentary (TSM) rocks. Although O, S, and Sr isotopes have suggested various degrees of contamination prior and syn emplacement, the contribution of assimilation of the TSM rocks to sulfide saturation and PGE-Ni-Cu values is still debated. In this study we use selenium isotopes for the first time in a layered mafic intrusion to assess the extent of crustal assimilation. Our results show a systematic increase in δ82/76Se values with depth, and ranges from 0.24 to 1.69 ‰, a trend similar to previously reported δ34S data from the same samples. The trend in δ82/76Se (and δ34S) with increasing depth is here interpreted as an indication of assimilation of crustal Se (and S) from the TSM rocks, suggesting that δ82/76Se (‰) can be used as a proxy for tracking crustal contamination in the Northern Limb of the BIC and elsewhere. Our study improves our understanding of the role of assimilation of the TSM rocks in the Northern Limb of the BIC by introducing Se isotopes as a geochemical tracer and demonstrates broader potential in understanding contamination processes in layered igneous intrusions.

title: Constraining the stable iron isotopic signature of easily reducible iron: the role of leaching time and extractant type
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Berenice Ebner, Susann Henkel, Katja Laufer-Meiser, Anette Meixner, Simone A. Kasemann, Male Köster, Sabine Kasten
abstract: Several approaches exist to quantify the easily reducible iron (Fe) pool in marine sediments and these methods are based on different operational definitions of Fe reactivity and easily reducible Fe phases. Ascorbate time-course extraction is one of these methods. Here, we present a novel protocol for processing of ascorbate time-course extracts for Fe isotope (δ56Fe) analysis and evaluate how leaching reagent and extraction duration influence measured δ56Fe values, compared to isotope data obtained from leachates with fixed reaction times. We compare δ56Fe signatures from time-course and classical end-point extractions to distinguish kinetic versus equilibrium fractionation and constrain the most representative δ56Fe composition of the easily reducible Fe pool in (sub-)polar marine surface sediments. In typical sequential extractions, the extraction is terminated at a pre-defined timepoint where the released Fe is quantified (end-point extractions), whereas in time-course extractions, the dissolved Fe concentration is monitored over time and the extraction is terminated when the extracted Fe reaches a plateau. Our study shows that depending on the size and heterogeneity of the easily reducible Fe pool in the sediment, the δ56Fe signature of the extracted Fe does not remain constant throughout extraction time and may be progressively modified by processes resulting in isotopic disequilibrium mixing. We propose that the δ56Fe value measured at the onset of the Fe concentration plateau provides the best operational approximation of the iron isotopic composition of the target pool, while a residual bias may remain where isotopic evolution continues beyond the inflection point.

title: Helium diffusion and (U-Th)/He thermochronology of pyromorphite
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Yan Ma, Finlay M. Stuart, Ying Wang, Jianzhang Pang, Lei Liu, Liene Spruzeniece
abstract: Pyromorphite [Pb5(PO4)3Cl], an end-member phase of the apatite group minerals, typically forms during supergene weathering of Pb-rich ore deposits. Uranium concentrations can reach several thousand ppm, making it a potential (U-Th)/He chronometer of weathering events and paleoenvironmental change. Here we present the first (U-Th)/He ages of pyromorphite and characterize He diffusivity through combined incremental heating experiments and first-principles density functional theory calculations. Two large gem-quality pyromorphite crystals from the Daoping mine (Guangxi, China) were selected for detailed study. (U-Th)/He ages measured in fragments of one crystal are over-dispersed, ranging from 0.06 Ma to 0.66 Ma, with a weighted mean of 0.33 ± 0.17 Ma. Incremental heating experiments reveal extremely high He diffusivity, with closure temperatures ranging from −79 to −27 °C for three aliquots. Density functional theory modeling suggests that Pb2+ (1.35 Å) expands interstitial sites in pyromorphite lattice in comparison to apatite (where Ca2+ is 1.18 Å) thus lowering the energy barrier for He diffusion. As- and V-substitution for P in the lattice expands a-axis parameters relative to pyromorphite, implying substantially lower helium closure temperatures for As- or V- bearing pyromorphite. Consequently, pyromorphite is unlikely to be suitable as a conventional He geo/thermochronometer. It may, however, hold value for paleotemperature reconstruction or as a host material for radioactive waste immobilization. The diffusivity of nucleogenic 21Ne is likely to be significantly slower than 4He implying that (U-Th)/Ne dating of high-U pyromorphite may be a promising alternative geochronometer for supergene lead mineralization, and ongoing work at SUERC is exploring this potential.

title: Enhanced productivity and phosphogenesis caused by renewed Middle Triassic upwelling along the northwestern margin of Pangea, British Columbia, Canada
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Cameron M. Wood, Stephen E. Grasby, David P.G. Bond, Yadong Sun, Benjamin M. Tutolo
abstract: The widespread occurrence of highly phosphatic black shales in Middle Triassic strata reveals a major transition in paleo-environmental conditions and resultant biological productivity. To establish whether this phosphatic interval was linked to a recovery in productivity following the Permian-Triassic Mass Extinction, we examined geochemical records of trace metal concentrations in sediments deposited along NW Pangea exposed in the Ursula Creek section on the shore of Williston Lake, British Columbia, Canada. Profiles of trace element paleo-environmental proxies were normalized to sedimentation rates to account for distortion by shifts in sedimentation. Our results show that an increase in seawater oxygenation and productivity during the Induan to lower Olenekian was short-lived. However, enhanced productivity in the Anisian to Ladinian was likely linked to a re-established connection with nutrients that had been trapped in deep ocean waters during the Early Triassic, when hothouse conditions suppressed upwelling. The phosphatic interval at Ursula Creek thus marks the resumption of nutrient upwelling and a corresponding recovery in productivity during the Middle Triassic. These findings indicate that widespread phosphogenesis observed in Middle Triassic strata archived the return of continental margin productivity.

title: Discriminating global ore deposit genetic types using chalcopyrite trace elements: Insights from interpretable machine learning
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Hong-Kai Li, Ming-Yu Cao, Ben Qin, Peng-Fei Wang, Le Wang
abstract: Chalcopyrite is the most widespread copper-bearing sulfide in Earth’s crust, the principal copper ore mineral, and an important recorder of ore-forming processes. Its trace-element composition provides valuable insights into deposit type and mineralization evolution, but the multidimensional relationships among numerous trace elements are difficult to resolve using conventional bivariate diagrams. Here, we develop an interpretable machine-learning framework for ore-deposit types classification based on chalcopyrite trace-element chemistry. A global dataset comprising 5,232 analyses from 232 deposits was compiled, covering nine genetic types across magmatic, hydrothermal, and sedimentary settings. We systematically evaluated workflows combining data transformation, class-balancing strategies, and classification algorithms. The final trained model achieved a balanced accuracy of 0.96. Feature-attribution analysis identified element-specific patterns consistent with established ore-forming processes and partitioning behavior. Nonlinear dimensionality reduction also revealed geologically meaningful genetic relationships among ore deposit types. From a comparative mineral-chemical perspective, the results also constrain trace-element incorporation in chalcopyrite under contrasting physicochemical conditions. Application of the trained machine-learning model to the Jiawula large Pb-Zn-Ag deposit in China supports an epithermal classification while indicating a genetic link with the southern porphyry stock, together defining a porphyry-epithermal system. Overall, interpretable machine learning offers a transferable framework for linking mineral chemistry, deposit classification, and metallogenic interpretation.

title: Influence of partial melting and ancient depletion on helium isotopes of mantle-derived magmas
description: Publication date: 20 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 722 Author(s): Andrea Giuliani, Senan Oesch, Federico Munch, Ronghua Cai, Jingao Liu, Mark D. Kurz, Peter H. Barry, Luc S. Doucet, Michael J. Walter
abstract: Several ocean island basalts (OIBs) exhibit less radiogenic He isotope ratios (i.e., higher 3He/4He) than mid-ocean ridge basalts (MORBs), as well as distinctive primordial and short-lived Ne and Xe isotope signatures. These isotopic features are generally considered to originate from long-term isolation of the deep-mantle source of these OIBs. However, global seismic tomography models have clarified that material exchange occurs between the upper and lower mantle via oceanic lithosphere subduction. This is consistent with the presence of subducted material in the deep-mantle sources of OIBs indicated by the radiogenic isotope compositions of lithophile elements (Sr, Nd, Hf, Pb). The origin of He isotope variations in mantle-derived magmas and especially the occurrence of highly unradiogenic He in some plume-related lavas remains, therefore, unclear. Considering negligible He recycling in the mantle via subduction, previous explanations for these ancient He isotopic signatures include melting of highly depleted sources, storage of primordial He in dense Fe-rich piles resulting from magma ocean crystallization, migration of solar-like He from the core to the lowermost mantle, or preservation of minimally processed, undegassed material in the deep convecting mantle. Here we show that high 3He/4He lavas from oceanic and continental settings predominantly derive from high degrees of melting as indicated by tholeiitic major element compositions, low concentrations of incompatible trace elements (Nb, Th) and low La/Sm ratios. Unradiogenic Sr and Pb combined with supra-chondritic Nd isotope compositions indicate that these lavas were derived from sources that have experienced minimal addition of recycled crustal material. However, these sources do not match ancient mantle domains (similar to FOZO) that are scattered throughout the convective mantle. This inference, combined with no clear relationship between He isotopes and 142Nd/144Nd anomalies, rules out the involvement of old and minimally processed convective mantle in the source of high 3He/4He lavas. The association of high 3He/4He lavas with seismically resolved conduits rooted in the lowermost mantle requires that unradiogenic He is stored in domains at the core-mantle boundary, possibly ULVZ (ultra-low velocity zones), which are exclusively tapped by the hottest and most buoyant plumes. Coupled with a correlation between He isotopes and 182W/184W anomalies, these observations suggest that unradiogenic He is delivered to peridotites in the lowermost mantle from either the core or dense residues of a basal magma ocean. In both cases, this high 3He/4He component exerts a negligible influence on the major and trace element compositions of the mantle source of oceanic and continental lavas with high 3He/4He, which is demonstrably peridotitic and moderately depleted in incompatible elements.

title: High precision water quantification by Raman spectroscopy: Applications to volcanic and extraterrestrial samples
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): E.G. Huggins, E. Gazel, M. Gavrilenko, K. Dayton, J.D. Bixler, W.H. Towbin, T. Plank
abstract: Volcanic petrology is a promising field to quantify processes that occur during eruptions, but it currently relies on very expensive and complex analytical techniques. Of particular importance is the development of precise, high spatial resolution techniques to measure volatile species (e.g., H2O, CO2, S) in volcanic glasses for understanding magmatic storage and eruptive potential. H2O controls the chemical and physical properties of magmas, impacting crystallization, viscosity, and buoyancy, and plays a significant role in the development of terrestrial planets. The predominant tools used to measure volatiles in volcanic glasses (as recorded in melt inclusions; MIs) typically require extensive and time-consuming sample preparation, and instrumentation is often not available in the timeframe of ongoing volcanic eruptions. Confocal Raman spectroscopy provides an alternative method that has been used successfully in recent years to quantify H2O contents of volcanic glasses and MIs with high spatial resolution, minimal sample preparation, and high throughput, such that samples can be analyzed within hours to days following sample collection. Here, we present high-precision calibrations for measuring dissolved H2O in silicate glasses by Raman spectroscopy using a high-energy 473-nm (blue) excitation source. To understand how this calibration compares to those derived from other microanalytical techniques, we analyzed reference glasses commonly used in different laboratories to calibrate volatile species. We then applied this calibration to exposed terrestrial MIs, melt embayments, and unexposed terrestrial and Martian MIs. The development of a method to measure water concentrations in unexposed MIs is critical for applications where preservation of rare samples is essential.

title: 40 Ar/ 39 Ar calibration of sanidine standards QSs and YBCs with Fish Canyon sanidine
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): Paul R. Renne, Brian R. Jicha, William S. Cassata, Roland Mundil, Andrew J. Tholt
abstract: ∼30 Ma (YBCs) and ∼ 120 Ma (QSs) sanidines are evaluated as 40Ar/39Ar standards in comparison with existing standards of similar ages. 40Ar*/39ArK ratios (F-values) in each relative to the widely used Fish Canyon sanidine (i.e. R FCs YBCs and R FCs QSs ) were determined on three different mass spectrometers. YBCs proved to have excess between-grain dispersion of F values and K/Ca, low %40Ar*, and is deemed to be inferior to the similarly-aged Taylor Creek sanidine (TCs) as a 40Ar/39Ar standard. QSs is significantly more reproducible at the single-grain level in terms of F values and K/Ca, and is recommended as an international standard in favor of the ∼99 Ma GA-1550 biotite. New CA-IDTIMS U-Pb data on zircons from the QSs host obsidian yield an inferred eruption age of 120.56 ± 0.26 Ma (2σ), indistinguishable from the sanidine 40Ar/39Ar age determined by the most recent 40Ar/39Ar-U-Pb intercalibration. Further radioisotopic analyses of both phases in other labs would be desirable in order to increase the utility of data from this sample for ongoing intercalibration efforts.

title: A lithium isotopic perspective of basalt weathering: Cycling of Li and its mobility relative to Ca and Mg
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): Anup Kumar Sharma, Tarun Kumar Dalai, Sambuddha Misra, Prem Chand Kisku, Jitendra Kumar Pattanaik
abstract: Lithium isotope compositions (δ7Li) are extensively utilized to trace silicate weathering and reverse weathering in both terrestrial and marine realms. Although the direction and magnitude of Li isotope fractionation during Li adsorption onto secondary minerals are well understood, the relative influence of Li partitioning via its adsorption vis-à-vis structural incorporation into clay minerals on overall Li isotope fractionation remains poorly constrained. In this study, we attempt to determine the processes regulating Li distribution and its isotope fractionation by quantifying the Li concentration and isotope ratio of the bulk, exchangeable, oxyhydroxide phases, and clay-sized fractions of two basaltic weathering profiles from the Rajmahal Volcanic Province (India). The observed decrease in δ7Li values toward the top of the weathering profiles, coupled with increases in Li/Al, Fe/Al, and Mn/Al ratios, indicates role of clay minerals and FeMn oxyhydroxides in the preferential adsorption and/or structural incorporation of 6Li. In the Dalahi profile, adsorption and desorption of Li exhibit possible pH dependency. Mass balance calculations demonstrate that crystal-bound Li in clay minerals dominates the total Li budget of the weathered basalts and therefore, drives the depth-dependent variation in δ7Li within the weathering profiles. There is excellent agreement between two independent calculations of δ7Li of weathering solutions, which are about 8.1–12.6‰ higher than that of the parent basalts. Notably, calculated δ7Li values for weathering solutions are within the range of δ7Li offsets observed between the rocks and solutions in river and groundwater systems in basaltic catchments. We established empirical relationships between δ7Li, mobility of Li relative to Ca and Mg, and the chemical index of alteration (CIA) in weathering profiles. These relationships provide a framework for reliable prediction of δ7Li and Li mobility relative to Ca and Mg during basaltic weathering. Additionally, by integrating published data on δ7Li and CIA in river sediments with the results of this study, we demonstrate that δ7Li values of river sediments can be predicted from their CIA values. The results and findings of this study provide new insights for investigating weathering processes in both modern and ancient records by using δ7Li as a tracer of weathering intensity and the relative mobilities of Li, Ca and Mg.

title: Sedimentary bacteriochlorophylls trace hypoxia and anoxygenic phototrophic carbon fixation on a river-dominated coastal shelf
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): Jiawei Kan, Liqin Duan, Jinming Song, Xue Liu, Xuegang Li, Huamao Yuan
abstract: Coastal hypoxia expansion may promote the growth of anoxygenic phototrophic bacteria (APB), thereby influencing the marine carbon cycle through anoxygenic photosynthetic carbon fixation (APC-F). However, APC-F in low-oxygen waters remains poorly constrained. Characteristic bacteriochlorophylls (Bchls) and carotenoids of APB may serve as an effective indicator of APC-F. This study investigated Bchls and carotenoids in surface sediments from the East China Sea coastal shelf, focusing on their sources, responses to hypoxia and water-column stratification, and potential use for estimating APB carbon fixation. The strong correlation between bacteriopheophytin a (Bphe a) and okenone, a characteristic carotenoid of purple sulfur bacteria (PSB), suggests that sedimentary Bphe a was mainly derived from PSB. Bphe a and okenone contents were approximately twice as high in mud sediments as in sandy mud and slightly sandy mud sediments. The negative correlations of Bphe a and okenone with bottom-water dissolved oxygen and their positive relationships with the salinity difference between surface and bottom waters indicate that these pigments are associated with low-oxygen conditions and water-column stratification. Based on Bphe a contents in surface sediments, APC-F was preliminarily estimated. The mean APC-F was 7.41 mg C/m2/yr in mud sediments and 1.47 mg C/m2/yr in sandy mud and slightly sandy mud sediments, and the maximum contribution of APC-F to total phototrophic carbon fixation reached 7.96%. Although absolute APC-F estimates are affected by uncertainties in pigment-to-carbon conversion factors, their relative spatial pattern still suggests an important role of APB in coastal carbon fixation.

title: Towards accurate Ca isotope fractionation at equilibrium between minerals and aqueous solutions with electronic structure calculations: Multi-framework comparison for validation and correction, and the control of structural cations
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): Merlin Méheut, Vasileios Mavromatis, Magali Benoît, Jacques Schott
abstract: Theoretical calculation of equilibrium fractionation of Ca isotopes shows particularly challenging due to the limitations of DFT frameworks to properly reproduce the important vibrational properties. This is even more challenging for mineral-solution equilibria, as frameworks adapted to minerals do not properly reproduce aqueous solution structures. Based on careful correction of calculated frequencies by experimental ones, a rescaling parameter can be proposed to obtain reference ln β values from eight different theoretical frameworks, within an uncertainty ( σ ) ranging between 0.25 ‰ (PBEsol and PBE functionals) and 0.75 ‰ (LDA functional, PBE or BLYP functionals with Grimme-D2 correction) at 300K. Frameworks showing more consistent structural prediction (with consistent offsets on Ca-O distances) also show more consistent predicted fractionation properties. Eight well characterized minerals (anhydrite, fluorite, diopside, grossular, calcite, dolomite, aragonite, CaO lime) were used for the validation and correction procedure, and six more (wollastonite, anorthite, huntite, monticellite, akermanite, gypsum) were calculated to infer the controls of Ca isotope fractionation and compare to experimental or natural estimates. Ca isotopes fractionation properties of a mineral shows connected to Ca-O distance, coordination and the type of structural cation, following the expression: (1) l n α m i n e r a l − C a O = l n β C a O × ( b × Δ d + c ( c o o r d ) + d ( c a t i o n ) ) , where α m i n e r a l − C a O is the fractionation of Ca isotopes with respect to CaO lime; β C a O is the β -factor of CaO lime; Δ d is the relative difference in Ca-O distance between the mineral and CaO lime; b=-7.44 at 300K; c is the coordination effect, varying monotonically from 0 for c(6) to ≈ +0.30 for c(8)=c(9); d is the effect of the cations present in the structure (in addition to Ca2＋), determined for Si 4 + , S 6 + , C 4 + , P 5 + (based on Antonelli et al. 2019’s calculations), and H + . The obtained cation effects appear to be related to their electronegativities. Assuming calcite-Ca2＋(aq.) fractionation as null, one can compare our predicted mineral-calcite fractionations with experimental mineral-Ca2＋(aq.) fractionations. The predicted aragonite-calcite and anhydrite-calcite fractionations are twice as large as the corresponding mineral-Ca2＋(aq.) experimental values, suggesting perturbing effects in solution (speciation, kinetic effects). On the contrary, predicted gypsum-calcite fractionations are in agreement with gypsum-Ca2＋(aq.) experimental values. Predicted dolomite-calcite fractionation agrees with fractionation occurring during biogenic dolomite precipitation, but dolomitization does not seem to follow isotopic equilibrium.

title: Flux-dominated crustal helium enrichment beyond Cratonic Basins: Evidence from geothermal fluids in the Cathaysia Block, South China
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): Xuelian Huang, Shuai Wang, Yunkai Lei, Xueqing Wu, Jingyu Lin, Xiangxian Ma, Wenjing Lin, Daniele L. Pinti, Guodong Zheng, Shihua Qi
abstract: Helium (He) is an irreplaceable resource for medical applications and high-end manufacturing. Global He production is currently dominated by He-rich natural gas accumulations in cratonic basins, whereas the origin and release–migration processes of He in active zones remain poorly constrained. This study investigates geothermal fluids from the Cathaysia Block (CB) in southern China, a representative tectonically reworked continental region, using newly collected and compiled gas and noble gas data (n = 217) to elucidate the formation of He-rich geothermal systems outside cratonic settings. He concentrations in the geothermal gases range from 10 to 18,300 ppm, and He-rich samples (He >1000 ppm) are consistently characterized by N2-dominated compositions. He concentrations are systematically higher in the inland domain than in coastal areas, and extremely He-rich fluids (He >10,000 ppm) occur exclusively in areas adjacent to Precambrian crustal relics. He isotope ratios (0.04–2.28 Rc/Ra) indicate minor mantle contributions, while radiogenic crustal He dominates (67.2–99.7%). Compositional and isotopic relationships in He–CO2–N2 system suggest that He enrichment is jointly controlled by CO2 removal and the addition of He-rich deep fluids. Regional thermal anomalies and seismic activities enhanced the mobilization of He accumulated in both Yanshanian high-radioactivity granites and Precambrian continental fragments, while deep major faults act as efficient migration pathways. Overall, the He-rich geothermal system in the CB exhibits the characteristics of an open crustal He flux system, defined by favorable source rocks, enhanced release, rapid migration, and limited preservation. Under suitable sealing conditions, such systems may also have He accumulation potential in sedimentary basins (e.g., the Sanshui Basin). Our results demonstrate that tectonically active regions can host flux-dominated crustal He systems and highlight the need to expand He exploration beyond conventional cratonic basins to tectonically reworked continental margins worldwide.

title: Bromine solubility in silicate melts and its implications for volcanic HBr degassing
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): Lauren R. Gorojovsky, Richard W. Thomas, Bernard J. Wood
abstract: We have determined the solubility of bromine in silicate melts using Ag-AgBr(±AgI) buffers to control fBr2, together with C-CO-CO2 and Re–ReO2 buffers to control fO2 over a broad range of melt compositions at 0.5–2.5 GPa and 1200–1500 °C. In the dilute region, melt Br concentrations vary with fB r 2 0.5 and f O 2 − 0.25 , consistent with dissolution through the exchange of two Br− ions for one O2− ion, analogous to the mechanism proposed for chlorine. Henry's law behaviour extends to 1.1 wt% Br, well above concentrations in natural melts. We use these relationships to define bromide capacity and, by combining our results with published hydrous fluid-melt partitioning data, derive a model applicable from 790 to 1500 °C and pressures up to 2.5 GPa. The resulting equation is: log C Br = 3.94 + − 972 X SiO 2 + 3360 X FeO tot + 3382 X CaO − 659 X H O 0.5 + 201 X Na O 0.5 − 11 X K O 0.5 − 1277 P − 6322 / T where T is in K, P in GPa, and Xi denotes single cation oxide mole fraction. Bromide capacity decreases with increasing pressure and temperature, decreases with increasing SiO2 and K2O contents, and increases with CaO and FeO, so that bromine solubility decreases in the order basalt > andesite > dacite > rhyolite. Bromide capacity is lower than chloride capacity for all compositions investigated, showing that bromine is consistently less soluble than chlorine in silicate melts. Despite this lower melt solubility, application of the bromide capacity model to H2O-rich low-pressure fluids indicate that Br and Cl degas similarly as HBr and HCl, respectively, so the HBr/HCl ratio of volcanic gases should closely reflect the Br/Cl ratio of the melt with little fractionation. These results provide a thermodynamic framework for modelling bromine behaviour in magmatic and volcanic systems.

title: Carbonate precipitation and CO₂ sources in a Hypersaline Crater Lake of the Pali Aike Volcanic Field, Southern Patagonia
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): Carolina Henríquez, Raphael Pietzsch, Leonardo Fadel Cury, Paulo Quezada, Guido Alonso, Luis Mancini, Mauricio Calderón, Anelize Bahniuk
abstract: Carbonate precipitation in southern high-latitude environments remains poorly constrained in terms of its controlling mechanisms, particularly in continental settings where climatic extremes, volcanic substrates, and inherited glacial processes converge. Here we investigate carbonate formation in an alkaline lake hosted within Middle Pleistocene maars of the Pali Aike Volcanic Field, southern Patagonia. This setting provides a natural laboratory to investigate interactions between silicate weathering, carbon cycling, and CaCO₃ supersaturation. Mineralogical and geochemical data, including 87Sr/86Sr, δ13C, and δ18O, from carbonates, basalts, soils, sediments, and lake waters were used to constrain the processes controlling carbonate precipitation. The δ13C composition of dissolved inorganic carbon (DIC) indicates that silicate weathering involving soil-derived and atmospheric CO₂ is the primary source of carbon to the lake system. Carbonate speciation reveals a strong dominance of HCO₃− and CO₃2− over dissolved CO₂ in the lake carbon pool. Strontium isotopic compositions identify mafic rock weathering as the principal source of dissolved Ca. Combined evidence from Sr partitioning, weathering indices, aqueous geochemistry, and stable isotopes indicates carbonate precipitation under sustained supersaturation, modulated by kinetic constraints rather than simple equilibrium conditions. These results define an integrated geochemical framework in which silicate weathering intensity, carbon cycle dynamics, and precipitation kinetics jointly regulate carbonate formation, with implications for interpreting lacustrine carbonate archives in high-latitude continental systems.

title: Ca isotope fractionation during precipitation of authigenic carbonates: A case study from the Haima cold seep, northern South China Sea
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): Jingya Cao, Junming Zhou, Junxi Feng, Jun Tao, Jie Xuan, Shengxiong Yang
abstract: Calcium isotopes serve as a sensitive tracer for carbonate formation processes, yet the mechanisms governing Ca isotopic fractionation during authigenic carbonate precipitation, particularly in dynamic cold-seep systems, remain debated. This study presents integrated elemental (Sr/Ca and Mg/Ca) and isotopic (C-O-Sr-Ca) data from two types of authigenic carbonates (chimney and shell-bearing) recovered from the two sites with high methane flux in the Haima cold seep, northern South China Sea (SCS). The chimney carbonates exhibit strongly negative δ13CV-PDB values of −33.3‰ to −30.1‰ and positive δ18OV-PDB values of 3.62–4.31‰, whereas the shell-bearing carbonates exhibit δ13CV-PDB values of −45.2‰ to −42.1‰ and δ18OV-PDB values of 3.85–4.34‰, confirming their methane seepage-related carbon and oxygen origin. Most of the samples show elevated Sr/Ca and depleted Mg/Ca mass ratios, consistent with a predominantly aragonitic composition, though a minor subset is calcite-dominated. It is indicated that Sr/Ca and Mg/Ca ratios are mostly controlled by the carbonate mineralogy rather than the precipitation rate. The 87Sr/86Sr ratios (0.709178–0.709278) of these authigenic carbonates closely match modern seawater signatures, indicating that authigenic carbonate formed within high methane flux shows significant potential for preserving the 87Sr/86Sr signature of ancient seawater. Calcium isotope compositions (δ44/40Ca) range from 0.73‰ to 1.37‰ and show strong correlations with Mg/Ca (positive) and Sr/Ca (negative) ratios, suggesting that carbonate mineralogy exerts a primary control on Ca isotopic fractionation. These findings highlight the pivotal role of carbonate mineralogy in governing the Sr and Mg concentrations and Ca isotopic signatures of authigenic carbonates in cold seeps.

title: First oxygen isotopic data of coexisting glauconite and celadonite by NanoSIMS
description: Publication date: 5 October 2026 Source: Chemical Geology, Volume 721 Author(s): Elisa Laita, Maria Àngels Subirana, Dirk Schaumlöffel, Matías Reolid, Isabel Abad, Fernando Nieto, Blanca Bauluz
abstract: This study presents the first nanoscale secondary ion mass spectrometry (NanoSIMS) oxygen isotopic analyses in coexisting glauconite and celadonite related to hydrothermal alteration of Jurassic pillow-lavas from the Subbetic (Betic Cordillera, South Spain). The slight differences in Fe and K content of these two micas allowed them to be differentiated by focused ion beam scanning electron microscopy (FIB-SEM) and extract them as separate 10 × 5 μm size and 1 μm thick lamellae of each mineral. This sample preparation eliminated the need of preliminary elemental mapping by NanoSIMS to identify the different minerals within the sample before the isotopic mapping. However, the small thickness of the studied lamellae caused their fast consumption during oxygen isotopic mapping. Together with the H-isotope fractionation that micas can undergo during heating and dehydroxylation this could prevent the later acquisition of deuterium measurements. NanoSIMS reported an average 18O/16O ratio for glauconite of 2.05 × 10−3 (±1.14 × 10−5), whereas the average ratio for celadonite was 2.02 × 10−3 (±1.43 × 10−5).
